topics.topic_name: Uninformed Search (BFS, DFS, Uniform-Cost Search, Iterative Deepening, Bidirectional Search)

resources.title: COMPSCI 188 - 2018-08-28 - Uninformed Search
resources.why_recommended: The canonical UC Berkeley CS188 lecture (Abbeel/Klein) on uninformed search - develops BFS, DFS, uniform-cost search and iterative deepening with the tree-search/graph-search framework and completeness/optimality analysis GATE tests.

resources.title: [CS188 SP24] LEC02 - Search: State Spaces, Uninformed Search
resources.why_recommended: A cleaner, more recent CS188 rendering of state-space formulation and uninformed search (BFS, DFS, UCS, IDS) with modern slides - excellent as an alternative or supplement to the Abbeel/Klein lecture.

resources.title: Artificial Intelligence - Search Methods for Problem Solving (IIT Madras)
resources.why_recommended: An entire NPTEL course devoted to search, with early modules building state-space search and the uninformed strategies (BFS, DFS, DFID/iterative deepening) in the theorem-oriented depth expected for GATE.

resources.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach (AIMA), 4th ed. - official book site
resources.why_recommended: The standard AI reference; Chapter 3 (Solving Problems by Searching) is the definitive written treatment of BFS, DFS, uniform-cost, iterative deepening and bidirectional search with complexity tables GATE quotes almost verbatim.

topics.topic_name: Informed / Heuristic Search (Greedy Best-First, A*, Admissibility, Consistency)

resources.title: COMPSCI 188 - 2018-08-30 - A* Search and Heuristics
resources.why_recommended: The gold-standard CS188 lecture on greedy best-first and A* search, carefully explaining admissibility vs consistency and why they guarantee optimality - exactly the distinctions GATE probes.

resources.title: [CS188 SP24] LEC03 - Search: Informed Search, A*, Heuristics
resources.why_recommended: A current CS188 walkthrough of informed search that builds heuristics, admissibility and consistency and the dominance of heuristics - a strong modern complement to the Abbeel/Klein lecture.

resources.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach (AIMA), 4th ed. - official book site
resources.why_recommended: Chapter 3's section on informed (heuristic) search is the definitive written source on greedy best-first, A*, admissible and consistent heuristics, and the proofs of A* optimality that GATE questions rest on.

resources.title: Artificial Intelligence - Search Methods for Problem Solving (IIT Madras)
resources.why_recommended: Khemani devotes several modules to heuristic search, algorithm A*, admissibility of A* and space-saving variations - rigorous, exam-oriented treatment of informed search.

topics.topic_name: Adversarial Search (Minimax, Alpha-Beta Pruning, Game Trees)

resources.title: MIT 6.034 Lecture 6: Search: Games, Minimax, and Alpha-Beta
resources.why_recommended: Patrick Winston's classic MIT 6.034 lecture builds game-tree search, the minimax algorithm, alpha-beta pruning and progressive deepening from scratch with memorable intuition - a standard reference for adversarial search.

resources.title: COMPSCI 188 - 2018-09-11 - Search with Other Agents: Minimax
resources.why_recommended: The CS188 lecture on minimax and alpha-beta pruning over game trees, with the resource-limited/evaluation-function view - directly aligned with GATE-style game-tree evaluation and pruning problems.

resources.title: COMPSCI 188 - 2018-09-13 - Search with Other Agents: Expectimax, Utilities
resources.why_recommended: Extends minimax to expectimax and utility theory, rounding out adversarial and stochastic-adversary search - useful context for game-tree questions beyond deterministic minimax.

topics.topic_name: Propositional Logic (Syntax, Semantics, CNF, Resolution, Satisfiability/Validity/Entailment)

resources.title: [CS188 SP24] LEC07 - Logic: Propositional Logic and Planning
resources.why_recommended: The CS188 lecture introducing propositional logic syntax and semantics, models, entailment, validity and satisfiability - the exact foundations GATE tests for propositional reasoning.

resources.title: [CS188 SP24] LEC08 - Logic: Logical Inference, Theorem Proving, Boolean Satisfiability, DPLL
resources.why_recommended: Covers inference by resolution, CNF conversion, the resolution rule and DPLL for satisfiability - precisely the CNF/resolution/SAT machinery GATE questions exercise.

resources.title: Logic 1 - Propositional Logic | Stanford CS221: AI (Autumn 2019)
resources.why_recommended: Stanford CS221's concise treatment of propositional logic - syntax, semantics, models, entailment and inference rules - a crisp complementary explanation to the CS188 lectures.

resources.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach (AIMA), 4th ed. - official book site
resources.why_recommended: Chapter 7 (Logical Agents) is the canonical written source for propositional syntax/semantics, entailment, CNF, the resolution algorithm and satisfiability - the reference GATE logic questions follow.

resources.title: [CS188 SP24] LEC09 - Logic: First Order Logic
resources.why_recommended: The CS188 lecture on first-order logic - predicates, functions, universal/existential quantifiers and inference - building the quantifier and unification concepts GATE examines.

resources.title: Logic 2 - First-order Logic | Stanford CS221: AI (Autumn 2019)
resources.why_recommended: Stanford CS221's focused explanation of first-order logic models, quantifiers and inference - a compact, high-quality supplement for predicate logic.

resources.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach (AIMA), 4th ed. - official book site
resources.why_recommended: Chapters 8-9 (First-Order Logic; Inference in FOL) are the definitive treatment of quantifiers, unification, forward/backward chaining and resolution in FOL - the source GATE predicate-logic questions draw from.

topics.topic_name: Bayesian Networks & Conditional Independence (DAG structure, joint-distribution factorization, d-separation)

resources.title: Bayesian networks (mathematicalmonk playlist)
resources.why_recommended: The mathematicalmonk Bayesian networks playlist is the clearest short-form derivation of DAG structure, joint-distribution factorization and d-separation / conditional independence - the go-to for understanding when variables are (in)dependent in a Bayes net.

resources.title: Bayesian Networks: Conditional Independences and d-Separation
resources.why_recommended: A focused walkthrough of reading conditional independences off a Bayes net via d-separation (chains, forks, colliders) - useful drill for the d-separation questions GATE asks. Video metadata (channel/duration) could not be fully verified from the page.

resources.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach (AIMA), 4th ed. - official book site
resources.why_recommended: Chapter 13 (Probabilistic Reasoning) develops the semantics of Bayesian networks, joint-distribution factorization via the chain rule and conditional independence relationships - the written foundation for this topic.

resources.title: COMPSCI 188 - 2018-10-16 - Bayes' Nets: Inference (Variable Elimination)
resources.why_recommended: The CS188 lecture on exact inference by variable elimination - factors, joining, marginalizing (summing out) and elimination ordering - the exact procedure GATE inference problems require.

resources.title: CS188 Fall 2018 (full course playlist)
resources.why_recommended: The complete UC Berkeley CS188 Fall 2018 playlist by Abbeel and Klein; its Bayes-nets sequence progresses from representation to exact inference by variable elimination, giving full context around the topic.

resources.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach (AIMA), 4th ed. - official book site
resources.why_recommended: Chapter 13's 'Exact Inference in Bayesian Networks' section formalizes enumeration and the variable elimination algorithm with factor operations and complexity discussion - the definitive written reference.

topics.topic_name: Approximate Inference — Sampling Methods (rejection sampling, likelihood weighting, Gibbs/MCMC)

resources.title: COMPSCI 188 - 2018-10-18 - Bayes' Nets: Sampling
resources.why_recommended: The CS188 lecture on approximate inference by sampling - prior sampling, rejection sampling, likelihood weighting and Gibbs sampling (MCMC) - covering exactly the four sampling methods in this topic.

resources.title: Machine learning (mathematicalmonk) - sampling / MCMC chapter
resources.why_recommended: mathematicalmonk's machine-learning series includes a dedicated sampling-methods chapter deriving rejection sampling, importance/likelihood weighting and Gibbs/MCMC with clean probabilistic reasoning - deeper theory than the CS188 lecture. Verify the exact sampling videos within the playlist.

resources.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach (AIMA), 4th ed. - official book site
resources.why_recommended: Chapter 13's 'Approximate Inference' section is the definitive written treatment of direct/rejection sampling, likelihood weighting and MCMC (Gibbs sampling) in Bayesian networks - the reference GATE sampling questions follow.
